To learn more please visit about GGGI web page. PURPOSE The primary objective of this position is to ensure GESI principles and Environmental and Social Safeguards are systematically integrated across the project's technical and financial components, from policy design through to guarantee facility implementation, grounded in a practical, technically informed understanding of the energy sector rather than a purely social-science lens. The role is critical in ensuring that biogas to biomethane investment benefits is broadly shared, including with women and community-based feedstock suppliers, and that the project's safeguard and exclusion criteria obligations are consistently met. By supporting GESI Assessment and Action Plan development, safeguards screening, and capacity-building, the position contributes to the overall success of GGGI's mission and the project's public-benefit objectives in Indonesia. ENGAGEMENT Support the development, implementation and monitoring of the project's GESI Assessment and Action Plan, in line with Donor's requirements and GGGI's GESI standards. Support screening of project activities and guarantee financed projects against the Donor and GGGI’s Safeguards Policy and Exclusion Criteria, flagging risks and proposing mitigation measures. Collaborate with Project team and BGF Fund Manager to design and deliver GESI training and capacity building as part of its readiness as the Facility's Fund Manager. Work with the project team to identify practical mechanisms for extending guarantee facility benefits to women and community led MSMEs involved in feedstock collection. Support the organization of stakeholder consultations, workshops and training sessions related to GESI and Environmental and Social Safeguards. Work in a confidential capacity and exercise sound judgement when handling sensitive safeguard-related information, including any complaints raised through the relevant mechanism. Collaborate with GGGI Indonesia's Energy team, contributing energy-sector technical perspective to team discussions and, as capacity allows, supporting technical inputs for the team's broader portfolio of energy projects. DELIVERY Contribute to the drafting, finalization and implementation of the project's GESI Assessment and Action Plan, aligned with the M&E Plan. Support Environmental and Social Safeguard and exclusion criteria screening for guarantee-financed biomethane projects, in coordination with BGF Fund Manager and participating banks. FUNCTIONAL Ability to develop and maintain strong relationships with GGGI partner institutions, including government counterparts. Ability to apply GESI and safeguard frameworks in a practical project context. Ability to work in an organized, systematic manner, with a degree of innovation and decision-making abilities. Ability to write concise and clear reports, GESI indicators, and meeting minutes, and to file them effectively to maintain the GGGI database. Ability to perform in a demanding atmosphere and self-motivate to produce quality results in a timely manner. Ability to communicate well with all stakeholders, including on sensitive safeguard-related matters. CORPORATE Understands and actively supports GGGI's mission, vision, and values. Promotes an organizational culture shaped by GGGI's values: Integrity, Excellence, Transformational, Inclusiveness, and Boldness. Promotes consistent integration of gender and social inclusion. Promotes the optimum use of resources; drives environmental sustainability at work. Manage emotions and stress positively, build rapport with the Country Team, and resolve conflict easily. Strong ability to work independently and/or remotely, while maintaining productivity. WORKING CONDITIONS GESI Associate is an G6 grade level in GGGI's National salary scale. Determination of base salary is subject to the candidate's experience, academic background, and internal equity. GGGI provides 15% of base salary towards retirement plan/long-term savings, 27 days of annual leave, and private health insurance that covers dental and vision. GGGI is committed to providing a work environment that is sufficiently flexible to accommodate diverse life-cycle challenges and assist Staff members to achieve a better balance between work and personal/family commitments, thus ensuring high performance, long-term productivity, and well-being of Staff members. The chosen candidate is expected to be based in Jakarta, Indonesia. This is a national position and does not include relocation benefits. PROJECT INTRODUCTION Based in Seoul, Republic of Korea, the Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) is an intergovernmental organization founded to support and promote a model of economic growth known as “green growth”, which targets key aspects of economic performance such a poverty reduction, job creation, social inclusion, and environmental sustainability. GGGI works with countries around the world, building their capacity and working collaboratively on green growth policies and green investment projects that can impact the lives of millions. The organization partners with countries, multilateral institutions, government bodies, and private sector to help build economies that grow strongly and are more efficient and sustainable in the use of natural resources, less carbon intensive, and more resilient to climate change. Currently, GGGI supports the Government of Indonesia (GoI) under the joint GoI-GGGI Green Indonesia Future Initiative Program (GIFT, “the Program”). The Program aims to demonstrate that green investments can become the norm both for investors and planners, ultimately improving the quality of economic development for more environmental sustainability and social inclusion. Through the Program, GGGI collaborates with the Ministry of Development Planning (BAPPENAS) as program host, the Coordinating Ministry of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources, Ministry of Environment, Ministry of Forestry, PT Sarana Multi Infrastruktur (“PT SMI”) , Indonesia Environment Fund (IEF), and others. Public benefits in this phase include building national institutional capacity to manage climate finance instruments, reducing systemic investment barriers, strengthening regulatory frameworks and creating the foundation for sustained methane emission reductions as well as green jobs creation.
